neighbours.label: the setup of a school maths exercise with quantities (word problems, area of a shape), as opposed to plain sentences about the same people and objects, with or without numbers, and to a question outside maths
fire: Sara has 36 stickers. She gives 1/3 of them to Ben. How many does she keep?
A triangle has a base of 10 cm and a height of 6 cm. Work out its area.
A bike costs $120 and sells for $90. How much was taken off?
There are 30 students in a class, and 2/5 of them are boys. How many girls are there?
A circle has a radius of 7 cm. Calculate its circumference.
Jake read 45 pages on Monday and 30 on Tuesday. How many pages did he read in total?
A tank holds 60 litres and is 3/4 full. How much water is in it?
The perimeter of a square is 28 m. What is the length of its side?
quiet: Sara turned 36 last May. She gave her old stickers to Ben when he moved.
The rectangle of lawn behind the house is long and narrow. Its edges need cutting.
The book costs more than I expected. With the new cover, it looks better.
There are many students in this class, and most of them are friendly. Their teacher is kind.
The circle of friends met on a Sunday. Its oldest member made tea.
Jake read 45 pages on Monday. Why did he stop there?
The tank sits behind the barn and is painted green. The water in it is cold.
The square in our town is 200 years old and has 12 trees. Its fountain was built in 1880.

short: setup of a school maths exercise
notes: Card: ' that' x6, ' of', ' the', 'ote', ' its', nearly all in maths exercises; gate-closed regime dominates and max is low (3.28). Probes: 0.38-0.76 on word problems, ' its' in shape problems 0.40-0.51; the same objects in plain prose 0.03-0.08. Pure maths statements are weaker: 'hypotenuse' 0.10, 'derivative' 0.04, 'Let x be' 0.15, tangent 0.18, and a train problem 0.14. 'asymptote' 0.52-1.31 is a separate strong token, not covered. The peak token varies and can come before any question (Oscar and Tom probes), so the label is about the setup, not about asking.
